exact_value.heading: Setup
exact_value.text:
1. Put the warp in the center. Each player takes five planets of one color, places four of their twenty ships on each, and places their colony marker beside the warp's 0 space.
2. Remove destiny cards naming unused player colors; shuffle the rest, including wilds and specials.
3. Shuffle the flares, deal two to each player, and give them the matching alien sheets. Each secretly chooses one alien, initially placing it facedown, and returns the other sheet to the box. This is the standard selection procedure; Hidden Powers is a separate excluded variant. The original text does not specify when standard-game sheets are turned faceup; unlike the optional Hidden Powers rule, it gives no explicit reveal window. This source gap is recorded rather than supplying a new setup rule. Green/yellow/red indicate recommended experience, not strength. Beginners may start with green aliens without flares.
4. Add **both flares dealt to every player**, including rejected aliens' flares, to the cosmic deck. Add random extras if needed to reach ten flares total; shuffle. Deal eight-card hands. Keep card faces private unless an effect allows showing them.
5. Draw destiny until a player color appears; that player starts. Shuffle the drawn card back into the destiny deck. Play passes left thereafter.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Card information, discards and exhaustion
evidence.text: If the cosmic deck runs out, reshuffle available discards. If a needed draw has no deck or discards, a **Cosmic Quake** makes everyone discard their hands; shuffle and deal eight to each player. If still insufficient, **Cosmic Aftershock** gathers all cosmic cards, including Miser's hoard and other set-aside cards, shuffles them, and replenishes Game Setup card holdings as at setup (including Miser's hoard). This is a needed-draw exhaustion rule, not an optional hand refresh.

evidence.heading: Overview
evidence.text: This summary covers the original **Fantasy Flight English 2008 CE01** game for 3–5 players, including its fifty original aliens, normal flare system and applicable official FAQ rulings. Optional Technology, Four Planets, Hidden Powers, Rotating Powers and Freewheeling Flares are excluded, as are Anniversary bonus content and all expansions. Read an individual card's printed effect and timing when playing it; the flare rules below explain the shared system rather than reproduce every flare card.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Original fifty alien reference / Reincarnator
evidence.text: **FAQ p19; retained official May6 2009 FAQ p1:** The Reincarnator flare's corrected timing is after the end of the encounter, so it does not stop a same-phase power use during the encounter. Its Wild targets another player, never yourself. You cannot use the Super flares of your incarnations. Corrected Wild: after another player besides Reincarnator loses or fails a deal, you may give them this flare. Immediately after the encounter they discard their current power and draw a new one, rejecting Game Setup or disallowed aliens and drawing again.

evidence.heading: Actions / Negotiate against negotiate: making a deal
evidence.text: Both sides' allies return ships to their own colonies, gain nothing and cannot participate in the deal. The main players have **one minute**. They may transfer cards from their hands and/or each grant the other **one colony on a planet where the giver already has a colony**, including a foreign colony. The recipient can use any own ships not in the warp. Existing ships coexist; the giver need not vacate, and vacating would eliminate the colony being offered. Return any remaining gate ships to offense's colonies.

evidence.heading: Turn Structure / 3. Launch
evidence.text: Defense cannot add or subtract ships on the target. The owner of a home system defends their planet even with zero ships there. Other colors' colonies are **bystanders**: they add nothing to the defense and the encounter result does not harm them. When driving out a foreign colony, target only that one color's colony; all other colors are bystanders.

evidence.heading: Turn Structure / 3. Launch
evidence.text: The offense chooses one planet in the destiny-indicated system and aims the gate at it. Place one to four offense ships on the **wide end of the hyperspace gate**, drawn from any combination of the offense's existing home and foreign colonies. You may strip a colony, but removing its last ship immediately eliminates it. Ships returning from an encounter or warp cannot return to that now-empty location as though it remained your colony.

evidence.text: At Planning, a defense lacking encounter cards reveals/discards the remainder and draws eight cards, repeating until it has an encounter card. An offense that runs out later in its turn **when it needs to play an encounter card** ends its turn instead of drawing a replacement. exact_value.text:

This counts as a win and successful encounter, proceeds only through Launch, and can qualify you for a second encounter.
- Wild: choose another player and encounter them in their home system.
- Special: follow its conditions, defense and location. The original rulebook's illustrated special card chooses the other player with the most current foreign colonies, excluding offense. Break a tie toward offense's left, choosing the first tied eligible player there; encounter that player in their home system (rulebook p7). For color-dependent effects such as Shadow, treat it as the designated defense's color.

evidence.heading: Setup
evidence.text:
1. Put the warp in the center. Each player takes five planets of one color, places four of their twenty ships on each, and places their colony marker beside the warp's 0 space.
2. Remove destiny cards naming unused player colors; shuffle the rest, including wilds and specials.

exact_value.heading: 3. Launch
exact_value.quote:
### 3. Launch

The offense chooses one planet in the destiny-indicated system and aims the gate at it. Place one to four offense ships on the **wide end of the hyperspace gate**, drawn from any combination of the offense's existing home and foreign colonies. You may strip a colony, but removing its last ship immediately eliminates it. Ships returning from an encounter or warp cannot return to that now-empty location as though it remained your colony.

Defense cannot add or subtract ships on the target. The owner of a home system defends their planet even with zero ships there. Other colors' colonies are **bystanders**: they add nothing to the defense and the encounter result does not harm them. When driving out a foreign colony, target only that one color's colony; all other colors are bystanders.

If you cannot put any ship in the gate or the last offensive ship is removed, continue the encounter. Winning alone does not give offense a colony without a ship to land, unless a specific effect allows it.

complete_original_entry.answer: Compensation is one card per main player ship actually lost to the warp: three cards. Allied losses do not count. Take randomly from the opponent’s hand without seeing faces; if fewer than three cards are held, take the entire hand. Evidence: E1, E2.

evidence.heading: Attack against negotiate: compensation
evidence.quote:
### Attack against negotiate: compensation

The negotiate player automatically loses; resolve the winner's ship destinations normally. The losing main player randomly takes one card from the opponent's hand for each of **their own ships actually lost to the warp**. Exclude allied losses: allies receive no compensation. If the opponent lacks sufficient cards, take the entire hand. Cards are taken without seeing their faces. Compensation is stolen hand cards; defender rewards are deck draws and/or warp retrieval.

No compensation for ships prevented from reaching the warp (Zombie/Observer) or removed by Void. Healer returning ships **after** they enter the warp does not remove compensation eligibility. Special winners such as Human/Pacifist can change who wins; compensation still requires the relevant attack-versus-negotiate condition.

evidence.heading: Pacifist
evidence.quote:
#### Pacifist

**Peace — Main player only; mandatory; Reveal.**

- If you reveal negotiate and opponent attack, use power to win encounter.
- If both reveal negotiate, attempt deal as usual.

**FAQ pp15,18:** Against zapped Human, the first conflicting win effect in normal timing order wins. If Loser calls an upset while you must reveal negotiate, you receive compensation only if Loser revealed attack and your ships actually reach warp.

exact_value.heading: Negotiate against negotiate: making a deal
exact_value.quote:
### Negotiate against negotiate: making a deal

Both sides' allies return ships to their own colonies, gain nothing and cannot participate in the deal. The main players have **one minute**. They may transfer cards from their hands and/or each grant the other **one colony on a planet where the giver already has a colony**, including a foreign colony. The recipient can use any own ships not in the warp. Existing ships coexist; the giver need not vacate, and vacating would eliminate the colony being offered. Return any remaining gate ships to offense's colonies.

A successful deal must actually transfer at least one card or colony; it may be one-sided. You cannot agree to do nothing. Tangible terms are restricted to permitted cards/colonies and specific power/card exceptions such as Zombie's liberation; future promises are unenforceable. Card terms may be explicit or vague but must be truthful and honored (if you promise your highest attack, give it). If time expires without agreement, **each main player loses three ships of their choice to the warp**, and offense cannot take an ordinary second encounter. Successful deals qualify for an ordinary second encounter but do not trigger win-only powers.

exact_value.heading: Start Turn and hand replacement
exact_value.quote:
### Start Turn and hand replacement

Start Turn occurs only before the first encounter of your turn, before Regroup effects. If offense has no encounter cards, reveal and discard the remaining hand, then draw eight new cards. You may first play legally playable non-encounter cards but are not required to play them. Hate draws a needed starting hand before using its power.

At Planning, a defense lacking encounter cards reveals/discards the remainder and draws eight cards, repeating until it has an encounter card. An offense that runs out later in its turn **when it needs to play an encounter card** ends its turn instead of drawing a replacement. Offense returns its committed ships to its own colonies; each ally returns that ally's committed ships to that ally's own colonies. The normal no-colony relocation rule applies. There is no automatic draw at the end of an encounter or turn, or merely for running out of cards. Alien and card effects can grant different draws.
